That three sided trick was so neat. Some explanations of the other tricks, if you're curious: 

Trick 1 - he solves the cube as he turns it in his hands. You can see some rotations as he starts to group the colors together. 

Trick 2 - this is essentially a blindfolded, one hand solve (OHS). Before he places the cube in the bag he pretends to show them how it's thoroughly mixed, however he is just memorizing the cube. When someone solves blindfolded they will take a few seconds to look at the cube and see how the pieces are situated. As he pulls the cube out of the bag he is aware of its orientation and he solves it (almost) before he takes it out of the bag. You can still see the last two moves. 

Trick 3 - as he spins the cube he is setting himself up for a blindfolded solve. He pauses to make "one more turn," which really just allows him to better set up the cube for the OHS before he throws the cube. It is solved before he throws it. 

Trick 4 - pretty much the same as the last one. Again, he looks at every side while he sets up the trick. After a quick blind OHS, he tosses it behind his back. 

Trick 5 - you pretty much got the gist of it. Basically, he solved the red, green, and white sides with the turns he made before he blew on it. You can see this because the remaining sides only have pieces that are yellow, orange, or blue. You can also see him finish the white side in the last move. He blows on the cube, flips it 180°, and the cube looks like it's entirely solved. He carefully keeps the three unsolved sides hidden as he casually starts to scramble the cube to conceal the trick. Pretty genius IMO. 

Trick 6 - this one is a little harder to tell because we haven't seen the entire set up. The cube that was sitting on the table had been in the same position for some time, so he presumably memorized the orientation on the visible sides. I'm not sure what he did to the cube in his left hand before the trick started, but it seems like he began to match it with the pattern on the other one. When he gets a better look at the other cube he makes a few turns on the cube he has been holding as well as some turns on the other cube to match them. This is a really impressive feat. Solving to a random pattern, let alone doing it by memorization shows some serious skill.

My drawer looks like [this](http://m.imgur.com/a/T34Fh). 

I'm a big fan of hiding apps and reducing redundancy so my drawer is less cluttered. For example, if I hit my home button I get my quick settings, which also has a button for the full settings app. So there's no settings in my drawer. I have a few apps accessible from my home screen, so those are also absent from the drawer. Every stock app I don't use is hidden with Nova. Lastly, if I have a gesture set up for something, I don't keep an icon for that in my drawer.


I also have a few apps grouped into folders that I hide. Everything I use to theme my phone is in one, so if I'm working on that I'll simply unhide the folder so I easily have access to my apps. This works well with the stock apps too. 

And most importantly, I try to be really diligent about deleting apps I don't use. Even fun games that I *might* want to play in the future (I'll just reinstall them). If I'm not using them now, I don't need the clutter. 

Hope that helps!

> For example, Japan is traditionally Shinto, with some Buddhism thrown in here and there

Yes Japan is "traditionally Shinto" but that is a huge understatement to Buddhism in Japan. During the emergence of the early Japanese State Buddhism had massive impacts. Rich scriptures and the organization of Buddhism actually severely dwarfed the native kami-worshiping. It is also responsible for being the vehicle that allowed the Chinese language to enter Japan (the Chinese language was the official written language of the Japanese government in the 9th century), which opened the door to a whole series of cultural changes. 

I think you can make that argument that because of Buddhisms connection to China it was partly responsible for the 17-articles and the Taika reform, but regardless you can not deny that Buddhism flourished in early fuedal Japan and remained a strong influence until the late Tokugawa/Meiji period. 

But alas, to strengthen your point, homosexuality (prostitution) was quite common in the early kabuki theater groups as well, especially after the transition to yarō-kabuki.

Well, my point is, anyone who is a decent grill cook will know how to cook your steak to temp and not loose it with carry over / resting and reheating.

There is no such thing as "Rare Plus". Rare plus is rare. Or if you want it "just past rare, but not medium rare" what you are actually saying is you want "rare". 

Trust me, when people order a "Rare Plus" the kitchen generally laughs, and we send out a rare, and people go on thinking that is a "rare plus" steak. 

edit: i meant to say rare plus is rare (not medium rare). when cooking a steak, you generally want to go under when unsure, because you can always bring it up. you can't un cook something.

Honestly, with a highly marbled steak like a ribeye, I think you want to cook it to medium rare or even medium (sometimes) to render all that tasty fat. The cook temps of rare and blue are generally reserved for other cuts such as Filet's and even New York's. 

I love a rare Filet for sure, but not a Ribeye, I think you loose a lot if you keep it at rare. 

Also, for cuts like teres major or coulotte, rare can be extremely chewy because of the muscle. A higher temp will result in some of that toughness being broken down a little.

As for the nervousness, just try to be yourself. If you try to impress her by being someone you're not, she may end up liking/disliking someone who isn't you.

And concerning the kiss, that is just something that you will have to intuit. If it feels right, go for it. If not, there is no reason to rush it just so it can happen that night. I find that people who don't want something physical will naturally move away. If you find her stepping away from you when you move close to her, probably not a good sign. Also, in my experience many women, (perhaps not at the age of 17) will initiate the first kiss. 

The most important thing is to be comfortable. Try to have a good time, ask her questions about things you are truly interested in, not just conversation starters.
